tools.name: search_norms
tools.description: Search Israeli building and planning norms by Hebrew words (substring search over norm texts, sections and document titles; norms in force come first). Returns norms with their permanent URL; call get_norm for the full text and citation.

tools.name: get_norm
tools.description: One norm by id: full Hebrew text, applicability, source document and section, dates in force, numeric values, exceptions, how its text was checked against print (print_check), and a ready citation line (cite).

tools.name: list_profile_options
tools.description: Valid codes for a project profile: uses, stages, cities (municipality slugs), plot conditions (sites), project elements (features), roles and requirement areas. Call before project_overview or project_requirements if unsure of a code.

tools.name: project_overview
tools.description: For a project profile (use, city, stage and optional details): how many norms apply, which depend on missing data or need a specialist, the next permit actions with their legal source, and which questions would narrow the list most. Every omitted detail keeps norms in (over-inclusive by design).

tools.name: project_requirements
tools.description: The norms that apply to a project profile, 50 per page, filterable by requirement area (e.g. fire, egress, parking, accessibility), by state and by Hebrew words. Texts are clipped; call get_norm for the full text.

tools.name: check_norm_for_project
tools.description: For one norm and a project profile: does it apply, why (by use, authority, stage) and which conditions could change that.

tools.name: permit_stages
tools.description: The building-permit process mapped to the stages of the Planning Administration's online system רישוי זמין, with the norms behind each step, plus how the database's texts were checked and the measured error rates. tools.name: source_changes
tools.description: What NORMOT's monitor detected in its sources (changed documents, expiring norms, latest Reshumot issues) and what was verified. With a profile, only documents relevant to that project.
